proves: A compliant name still produces one finding per token. A review can see why the name was accepted, not merely that it was, and the whole-name findings are absent because they are emitted only on failure.

The regression guard for the false-positive class. A rule that reads two to five capitals as an abbreviation flags all four of these English words and offers corrections for none of them; the allow lists are consulted first, so each one passes as a word and says so in its reason code.
TOTAL is in common_keywords and in short_full_words. The consult order decides which reason code is reported, and reporting the earlier list is the decision - not an accident of set iteration.

ZIP is in none of the three allow lists; it is approved by its own keep_as_abbrev catalog row. Consulting the entry after the lists is what lets the verdict carry the proper-noun code rather than the blander approved-abbreviation one.

Three unapproved abbreviations, each with the approved form the catalog names, found by going through the long form: CUSTMR means Customer, Customer abbreviates to CUST. The whole-name finding carries a null token and its fix clears only itself - it appends and does not re-case.

Casing is a whole-name property and is judged separately from the tokens. Both tokens are approved on their merits; the name fails only for how it is written, and the fix re-cases without touching anything else.
An unknown token fails rather than being rubber-stamped, and its fix is null. The library will not propose a replacement the catalog cannot justify, so the finding says what is wrong and stops there.

Every token is approved and the name is still 32 characters against a 30-character ceiling. The result is the full name plus a finding: seven passing tokens are reported, none is dropped, and the fix is null because there is no governed rewrite that fits.
One bad token out of three is what a compliance failure usually looks like, which is why the verdict is never a bare boolean: the caller needs to know it is XYZ and not TXN or ID.
